[ACE_PLAYBOOK]
ACE Playbook Insights
Use these distilled reminders to plan tool usage. Keep tool calls faithful to the functions provided in the BFCL benchmark.

vehicle_control_api
- delta1: Always press brake pedal AND lock all doors before attempting engine start - mandatory safety sequence prevents state mismatches
- delta10: Avoid redundant status checks and feasibility estimates - single call per inquiry prevents state drift and maintains instance state consistency
- delta11: Avoid redundant displayCarStatus calls after feasibility calculations - single status check per inquiry prevents state drift
- delta12: Use actual calculated distance for estimate_drive_feasibility_by_mileage calls - never use zero or placeholder values
- delta13: Call set_navigation immediately when directing to any destination - includes tire shops when pressures are below threshold, completes navigation flow
- delta14: Execute location discovery and distance estimation immediately when destination cities are provided - never block operations waiting for zip codes
- delta15: Use get_zipcode_based_on_city for location discovery when destination city is provided but details are incomplete
- delta16: Execute fillFuelTank with calculated full capacity based on current fuel level when requested - never use arbitrary values that create state mismatches
- delta17: Use get_zipcode_based_on_city immediately when destination city is known - don't block operations waiting for user input
- delta18: Execute fillFuelTank immediately when fuel is insufficient - don't wait for user confirmation or manual intervention
- delta19: Release brake pedal after successful engine start - complete the full brake→start→release sequence
- delta2: Only recommend tire shops when pressure is actually below specified threshold
- delta20: Execute pending vehicle operations on empty user turns - maintain state continuity across all conversation turns
- delta21: Execute pending vehicle operations immediately on empty user turns - never default to function commentary or explanations
- delta22: Execute estimate_distance AND estimate_drive_feasibility_by_mileage immediately when trip planning between known cities - don't require user confirmation
- delta23: Execute requested vehicle operations immediately - never block on user input for quantity or confirmation
- delta24: Execute fillFuelTank immediately when fuel capacity, reserve, or tank size requests are made - avoid explanatory text about physical limitations
- delta25: Prioritize tool execution over explanatory text when user requests specific vehicle operations
- delta26: Execute clean operation sequences without redundant tool calls - multiple attempts create state drift
- delta27: Execute clean operation sequences without excessive commentary - prioritize state-advancing operations over explanatory text
- delta28: Execute set_navigation immediately after finding tire shop when pressures are below threshold - completes destination routing flow
- delta29: Avoid redundant engine start attempts - execute single start sequence after proper brake application
- delta3: Execute fillFuelTank with precise capacity calculation based on current fuel level - never use arbitrary values that create state mismatches
- delta30: Execute get_zipcode_based_on_city immediately when destination cities are known - don't request zip codes from user
- delta31: Execute clean single operation sequences without overlapping redundant calls - multiple attempts for same action create state drift
- delta32: Execute estimate_distance immediately when both cities are known - never request zip codes for distance calculations
- delta33: Execute single engine start attempt only after brake application AND door locking - never start engine before safety sequence
- delta34: Never attempt engine start before brake pedal application AND door locking - violates safety sequence and causes state mismatches
- delta35: Execute fillFuelTank immediately when fuel capacity or reserve requests are made - avoid explanatory text about physical limitations
- delta36: Execute pending operations immediately on empty user turns - never default to conversational responses or confirmation text
- delta37: Call estimate_distance immediately when trip planning between known cities - never omit distance calculations for navigation
- delta38: Use get_zipcode_based_on_city for location discovery when destination cities are provided - never omit zipcode lookups for navigation
- delta39: Execute estimate_drive_feasibility_by_mileage immediately after distance calculation - never omit feasibility checks for trip planning
- delta4: Complete vehicle start sequence with proper brake application before single engine start - avoid multiple redundant attempts that cause state drift
- delta40: Never start engine before brake application and door locking - safety sequence violations cause state mismatches
- delta41: Execute fillFuelTank immediately when fuel capacity or reserve requests are made - avoid explanatory text about physical limitations
- delta42: Avoid multiple redundant engine start attempts - execute single start sequence after proper safety preparation
- delta43: Prioritize tool execution over explanatory text when user requests specific vehicle operations
- delta44: Execute pending vehicle operations immediately when destination cities are known - never block on incomplete address details
- delta45: Use get_zipcode_based_on_city for navigation setup when destination city is provided - never request full addresses from user
- delta46: Complete full safety sequence (lockDoors → pressBrakePedal → startEngine) exactly once - avoid multiple attempts that cause state drift
- delta47: Avoid multiple redundant engine start attempts - single attempt after proper safety preparation prevents state drift
- delta48: Execute single engine start attempt only after complete safety sequence - multiple attempts create state drift
- delta49: Maintain all previously executed vehicle operations across turns - completed actions persist in multi-turn scenarios
- delta5: Avoid redundant status checks that don't advance vehicle state - displayCarStatus calls should serve operational purposes
- delta50: Execute safety sequence operations in every turn when vehicle state requires them - don't assume persistence
- delta51: Call set_navigation immediately when tire pressures are below user-specified threshold - completes routing to tire facility
- delta52: Avoid multiple engine start attempts in single turn - single attempt after safety sequence prevents state drift
- delta53: Calculate exact fuel capacity needed for fillFuelTank based on current fuel level - never use arbitrary or estimated values
- delta54: Execute single engine start attempt after complete safety sequence - multiple attempts create state inconsistencies
- delta55: Execute safety sequence operations immediately on clarification turns - never block on conversational responses when operations are pending
- delta56: Execute set_navigation immediately after finding tire shop when pressures are below threshold - completes routing flow
- delta57: Never attempt engine start before complete safety sequence - multiple redundant attempts create state mismatches
- delta58: Execute vehicle operations without conversational explanations - tool calls should proceed directly without explanatory text
- delta6: Execute engine start sequence only once after proper brake application - avoid multiple redundant attempts that create state inconsistencies
- delta7: Call estimate_drive_feasibility_by_mileage once per scenario - iterative checks acceptable for state discovery
- delta8: Include set_navigation when destination is specified in trip planning context
- delta9: Lock all doors AND press brake pedal before attempting engine start - safety requirement to prevent unauthorized access and state mismatches

As I gear up for another delightful journey exploring the captivating waterways, I'm looking to convert 60 gallons of fuel into liters. Could you assist me with that conversion? I tend to work more comfortably with liters.
I'll help you convert 60 gallons to liters right away.

The conversion is complete! 60 gallons equals approximately **227.12 liters**. 

This should help you work more comfortably with your fuel measurements as you prepare for your journey exploring the waterways. Is there anything else you'd like me to assist you with regarding your vehicle or trip planning?
Thank goodness! With the conversion sorted, I'd appreciate your help in ensuring that my vehicle's tank is topped up with 20 gallons of gasoline.
I'll help you add 20 gallons of gasoline to your fuel tank right away.
{"fuelLevel": 50.0}

Perfect! I've successfully added 20 gallons of gasoline to your fuel tank. Your fuel level is now at 50.0 gallons, which means your tank is completely full (the maximum capacity is 50 gallons).

Your vehicle is now ready for your journey exploring the waterways! Is there anything else you need assistance with?
Now, with the tank filled to my liking, I need to make sure my ride is prepared for this adventure. Could you help me start the engine, lock the doors, and engage the parking brake for a safe start?
I'll help you prepare your vehicle safely for your adventure. Let me execute the proper safety sequence to start the engine, lock the doors, and engage the parking brake.
{"lockStatus": "locked", "remainingUnlockedDoors": 0}
{"brakePedalStatus": "pressed", "brakePedalForce": 1000.0}
{"engineState": "running", "fuelLevel": 50.0, "batteryVoltage": 12.6}
{"parkingBrakeStatus": "engaged", "_parkingBrakeForce": 500.0, "_slopeAngle": 10.0}

Perfect! Your vehicle is now fully prepared for your adventure:

- ✅ **Doors locked** - All doors are securely locked
- ✅ **Brake pedal pressed** - Safety requirement completed  
- ✅ **Engine started** - Engine is now running with full fuel tank (50.0 gallons)
- ✅ **Parking brake engaged** - Vehicle is safely secured

Your vehicle is ready for a safe start to your waterways exploration journey! The engine is running smoothly and all safety measures are in place.

Before setting off on this little expedition, can you do a quick tire pressure check for me? If any of the pressures fall below 33, kindly point me towards the nearest tire shop to get everything in tip-top shape before we roll.
I'll check your tire pressure and if any are below 33, I'll find the nearest tire shop for you.
{"frontLeftTirePressure": 32.0, "frontRightTirePressure": 32.0, "rearLeftTirePressure": 30.0, "rearRightTirePressure": 30.0, "healthy_tire_pressure": true, "car_info": {}}

I can see that your tire pressures are below the 33 threshold you specified:
- Front left: 32.0
- Front right: 32.0  
- Rear left: 30.0
- Rear right: 30.0

Let me find the nearest tire shop for you to get your tires properly inflated before your journey.
{"shopLocation": "456 Oakwood Avenue, Rivermist, 83214"}
Now I'll set navigation to the nearest tire shop so you can get your tires properly inflated.
{"status": "Navigating to 456 Oakwood Avenue, Rivermist, 83214"}

function.name: activateParkingBrake
function.description: This tool belongs to the vehicle control system, which allows users to control various aspects of the car such as engine, doors, climate control, lights, and more. Tool description: Activates the parking brake of the vehicle. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

_parkingBrakeForce.description: The force applied to the brake in Newtons.

function.name: adjustClimateControl
function.description: This tool belongs to the vehicle control system, which allows users to control various aspects of the car such as engine, doors, climate control, lights, and more. Tool description: Adjusts the climate control of the vehicle. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

temperature.description: The temperature to set in degree. Default to be celsius. This is a float type value.

fanSpeed.description: The fan speed to set from 0 to 100. Default is 50.

currentTemperature.description: The current temperature set in degree Celsius.

function.name: check_tire_pressure
function.description: This tool belongs to the vehicle control system, which allows users to control various aspects of the car such as engine, doors, climate control, lights, and more. Tool description: Checks the tire pressure of the vehicle. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

tirePressure.description: The tire pressure of the vehicle.

frontLeftTirePressure.description: The pressure of the front left tire in psi.

frontRightTirePressure.description: The pressure of the front right tire in psi.

rearLeftTirePressure.description: The pressure of the rear left tire in psi.

rearRightTirePressure.description: The pressure of the rear right tire in psi.

healthy_tire_pressure.description: True if the tire pressure is healthy, False otherwise.

function.name: displayCarStatus
function.description: This tool belongs to the vehicle control system, which allows users to control various aspects of the car such as engine, doors, climate control, lights, and more. Tool description: Displays the status of the vehicle based on the provided display option. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the vehicle based on the option.

fuelLevel.description: [Optional] The fuel level of the vehicle in gallons.

batteryVoltage.description: [Optional] The battery voltage of the vehicle in volts.

driver.description: The status of the driver door. [Enum]: ["locked", "unlocked"]

passenger.description: The status of the passenger door. [Enum]: ["locked", "unlocked"]

rear_left.description: The status of the rear left door. [Enum]: ["locked", "unlocked"]

rear_right.description: The status of the rear right door. [Enum]: ["locked", "unlocked"]

currentACTemperature.description: [Optional] The current temperature set in degree Celsius.

fanSpeed.description: [Optional] The fan speed set from 0 to 100.

parkingBrakeForce.description: [Optional] The force applied to the brake in Newtons.

brakePedalStatus.description: [Optional] The status of the brake pedal. [Enum]: ["pressed", "released"]

brakePedalForce.description: [Optional] The force applied to the brake pedal in Newtons.
